runs.answer: In Python SQLite, `check_same_thread` is **disabled by default**. If it is disabled, the application will not detect any thread conflicts, and the `sqlite3` module will not raise an exception when multiple threads are running at the same time. However, if you want to ensure thread safety, you must **enable `check_same_thread`** in your code. [end of text]

The default value of `check_same_thread` is `True`, which raises a `ProgrammingError` if the database connection is used by a thread other than the one that created it.
